name: Evaluation Datasets
blurb: Benchmarks and test sets, and what each actually measures.

items.note: Grade-school math word problems; the standard arithmetic-reasoning test
Science exam questions in easy and challenge splits
57-subject knowledge exam; the most-cited general capability benchmark
Commonsense sentence completion designed to be adversarial to models
The successor suite to GLUE for language understanding
164 hand-written programming problems; the original code-generation benchmark
The harder ten-choice successor as frontier models saturated MMLU
Graduate-level science questions that resist search; gated to keep answers out of training data

reading.body:
GSM8K leads all evaluation datasets here with 1.15 million downloads, roughly twice the next closest, which signals that arithmetic reasoning is currently the most-tested capability in the field.

The download distribution is not uniform. GSM8K and ARC together account for more than half the total downloads across all nine datasets. MMLU, despite being the most-cited general capability benchmark, ranks third. MMLU-Pro, its harder ten-choice successor, exists precisely because frontier models saturated the original, and its 201,000 downloads suggest it is gaining traction but has not yet replaced MMLU as the default reference. That progression, from a benchmark to its harder successor, is the clearest pattern the data shows: tests become obsolete as models improve, and the field moves to harder ones.

Eight of the nine datasets are ungated. The exception is GPQA, which covers graduate-level science questions and is gated specifically to keep answers out of training data. That single design choice points to a genuine measurement problem: a benchmark loses validity if its questions appear in pretraining corpora, and the more downloads a dataset accumulates, the more likely it is to have been scraped and learned from. The data records download counts but cannot say how many of those downloads fed training pipelines rather than evaluation runs.

What the data does not cover is how any of these benchmarks connect to real-world capability or to the compute required to move scores on them. Download volume measures researcher attention, not benchmark quality or task importance.
